text:
maya: Heads up, I ran the long-context synthetic sweep on staging (2.1.0-rc1) against the kvcache stress harness and I'm seeing steady RSS growth over ~3h.

alex: How steady? numbers?

maya: ~350MB -> 1.9GB over 3h on a single worker (A100). Allocation graph looks like repeated small increments correlated with long requests (seq_len 64k). Not an immediate spike, more like creeping growth.

rachel: Did you run with the memory-reuse flags? kernel selection changes in rc1 could affect alignment/repacking.

maya: Ran with --reuse-kv=true and default quant-opt kernels. Disabled continuous batching to isolate. Re-ran with --reuse-kv=false and growth still present but ~30% slower.

alex: Any sign of eviction/paging churn? iostat / vmstat during the run?

maya: vmstat shows occasional swapin spikes when RSS crosses 1.6GB, but swap usage is small. kvcache metrics: evictions per minute increased linearly. Fragmentation metric (kvcache_free_frag_ratio) drifted from 0.12 -> 0.46.

sam: Can you paste the small repro command and the perf log snippet?

maya: Command:
```
./tools/run_kvcache_synth --model gpt-small --seed 17 --steps 120000 --seq-length 65536 --reuse-kv=true --report out/perf-1782106324.json
```
Log excerpt (trimmed):
```
[13:02:11] kvcache: alloc 64B chunk id=0x7f8a.. free_frag=0.12
[14:21:05] kvcache: alloc 512B chunk id=0x8b3c.. free_frag=0.29
[16:01:33] kvcache: evict candidate count=8, total_pages=1024
[16:11:02] mem: RSS=1900MB heap-objects=1.2M kvcache_frag=0.46
```

rachel: Hmm. That fragmentation trend + evictions suggests short-lived small allocations that aren't being coalesced. Could be an allocator regression or a new change in the compaction path from rc1.

alex: Does this reproduce on the previous release (2.0.7)?

maya: I ran 2.0.7 on a separate worker with the same harness and seed for 6h — flat RSS (within ~40MB). So regression introduced between 2.0.7 and 2.1.0-rc1. Bisect candidate: commit range a1b2c3d..f6e5d4c (kernel packing + kvpage bookkeeping change).

sam: Can you capture jemalloc/jmap stats at end of run? and a heap profile? We need to know if it's external fragmentation or internal bookkeeping.

maya: Got jemalloc stats and a tcmalloc snapshot. Attaching gist links: https://gist.company/jemalloc-1782106324 and https://gist.company/heap-1782106324

rachel: I scanned the jemalloc dump — retained memory per arena increased in small increments, and there's a cluster of ~256B free regions that are not being reused. That maps to the kvcache small-slab allocations.

alex: Hypothesis: recent change to page header padding + alignment for the new kernels increased internal fragmentation for small entries. If headers grew from 8->16 bytes, small entries become power-of-two bigger and fill slabs differently.

maya: Agree. I added a debug counter for header_size and saw it flip from 8->16 in rc1 runs.

sam: Good find. Quick mitigation: add fallback to old header packing when avg_entry_size < 128 bytes. We can ship as a short-term patch and add a regression test.

rachel: For the regression test, let's add a deterministic long-context job to the eng-runtime CI: run_kvcache_synth --seed 17 --steps 200000 --seq-length 65536 --reuse-kv=true. Fail if RSS growth > 25% or kvcache_free_frag_ratio > 0.35 after step 100k.

alex: Also add a perf baseline artifact uploader so we can track regressions across commits. Put artifacts under s3://redwood-perf/eng-runtime/kvcache/ and include the perf JSON.

maya: I'll open a PR with the mitigation + CI test. PR will include the repro script and the jemalloc dumps. Draft attached: https://git.company/redwood/infra/commitfix/PR-412

infra-bot: deploy-notify: staging deploy 2.1.0-rc1 at 2026-03-16T12:00:00Z by ops/ci

sam: After PR lands, let's run a 12h stability sweep on a small pool (3 workers) and compare fragmentation trajectories.

rachel: Agreed. Also add a unit test to exercise small-entry packing behavior to catch header_size flips in future.

maya: Thanks. I'll queue the PR and kick off the extended sweep once merged. cc @alex @sam :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks all. If someone can run the bisect (a1b2c3d..f6e5d4c) and report which commit toggles header size that's priority one.

maya: Will run the bisect today and post results in this thread.

sam: Sweet. keep updates short here.

maya: Bisect result: commit f2d3e4b toggles header packing (PR: change-kv-header-padding). Reverting that commit in a local build removes RSS growth. I'll include the revert/conditional in the PR.

rachel: Nice. Once PR is in, schedule a canary on dedicated capacity and monitor token-level latency impact (should be none).

maya: PR created: https://git.company/redwood/infra/pull/418 — includes test + patch. Marking as ready for review.

alex: Reviewing now.

maya: Last note: added a short doc snippet in the PR explaining how to run the harness and interpret kvcache_free_frag_ratio.

sam: Perfect. We'll close the loop after the 12h run.
